bullets.text: In Chennai, power cuts continued in the city and its suburbs with several residential neighbourhoods reporting outages that lasted hours.
Near Velachery, a car caught fire suddenly on the road, causing a traffic stir and leading police to investigate the incident.
In Thiruvallur, the public staged a road roko protest due to sudden power cuts affecting normal life and local movement.
The state highways department began desilting and clearing three culverts along Jawaharlal Nehru Salai near Velachery MRTS station to improve storm water discharge.
Anbumani Ramadoss inspected the three-kilometre boundary wall and walkway construction work being carried out by the Tamil Nadu government in the Pallikaranai marshland.
Police arrested a maid and her lover for allegedly stealing a suitcase, gold jewellery, and cash from a doctor's apartment in Puzhuthivakkam, Pallikaranai.
In Thiruvallur, an alert police officer rescued a young woman from a dangerous railway track incident, drawing widespread praise.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched development projects worth over Rs 13,000 crore across Tamil Nadu during his visit.
Water was released from the Poondi reservoir through a link canal to Puzhal and Chembarambakkam reservoirs to meet Chennai drinking water needs.
Tamil Nadu is seeing a turnaround in its global capability centre story as existing centres expand and new setups continue to arrive.
Housing and Urban Development Principal Secretary R Kirlosh Kumar announced that SPEED, an AI-based planning approval software, will soon be introduced.
Amazon is reportedly in talks to acquire artificial intelligence startup Decart for approximately $7 billion.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid foundation stones for various infrastructure and development projects worth Rs 13,000 crore in Chennai.
During the IIT Madras event, Prime Minister Modi advised students to treat the Thirukkural as a guide and carry Tamil culture wherever they go.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi reaffirmed his commitment to Tamil Nadu development and praised cooperative federalism during his visit.
